name: FullEnrich
summary: B2B contact enrichment with waterfall data. Find verified emails and direct phone numbers for prospects by combining 20+ data providers in one lookup.
best_for: outbound teams that need maximum find-rates on emails and especially mobile numbers, and prefer paying only for verified hits
skip_if: you only need emails at volume (single-source tools are cheaper per hit), or your ICP data lives fine in one database already
honest_knock: The pay-on-success model is refreshingly honest, but note the 10x: phone numbers eat credits ten times faster than emails, so a calling-heavy motion consumes budget quickly: model your email/phone mix. As a waterfall over 20+ providers, its hit rate beats single databases; the flip side is you're paying a premium per contact versus querying one source that might have sufficed.

pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-09-23 against the vendor's own pricing page and its machine-readable pricing file fullenrich.com/pricing.md, which declares USD) Credit-based, and credits are spent only when data is found and passes verification: a failed lookup costs 0 and a landline returned instead of a mobile costs 0. Credit costs, unchanged: work email 1, personal email 3, mobile phone 10, reverse email lookup 1, a person-plus-company profile 0.25 on its own and free alongside any enrichment. Free trial: 50 credits, no card, more for inviting team members. Pro monthly, per the vendor's own table: 500 credits $29 ($0.058 each), 750 $42.75, 1,000 $55 ($0.055), 1,500 $79.50, 2,000 $104, 5,000 $255, 10,000 $499, 15,000 $720 ($0.048), 25,000 $1,150, 50,000 $1,950 ($0.039), 100,000 $3,500 ($0.035), above that contact sales. Pro annual (~10% cheaper, credits granted per year): 6,000/yr $312 ($26/mo, $0.052), 9,000 $468, 12,000 $588, 18,000 $852, 24,000 $1,128, 60,000 $2,784, 120,000 $5,448, 180,000 $7,860, 300,000 $12,552, 600,000 $21,228, 1,200,000 $37,800 ($0.032). Enterprise is custom. Unlimited users on every plan, no seat or platform fee. Credits roll over 3 months on monthly and 12 months on annual. CORRECTION 23 Sep 2026: this dossier previously gave Pro as 'from $55/mo'; $55 is the 1,000-credit step the slider opens on, and the ladder starts at $29 for 500. Reading note: from a Dutch exit the slider prints euros (EUR 0.055 a credit at 1,000) while the calculator's recommended-plan card prints $720/mo.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested FullEnrich with free credits: one enrichment of a fictional person at example.com and the billing page. No real person was enriched, so the hit rate for mobile numbers was not tested. Group 1, the hit rate on mobile numbers for outbound teams, is not tested: a hit rate can only be measured on real people and the test plan forbids enriching them. One fictional person at example.com was enriched with Mobile phone and Work email both ticked; company suggestions appeared while typing. Enrich 1 contact was pressed at about 17:23. The result page, Default List, showed Running while the status moved through sources (Enriched in the past 1/14, then Wiza 3/14). After about 3 minutes it showed Done 1/1 with Phone Not found, Work Email Not found, status Enriched and 0 credits used, and the sidebar still said 50 credits left. So a failed lookup, even one that included a mobile number at 10 credits, cost nothing in this run. This is one fictional record on a reserved example domain, so it says nothing about the find rate or about charges for partial hits. Download and Push to HubSpot were not used. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Only the work email option is ticked by default; the mobile phone option, at 10 credits, has to be ticked. The result for one record took about 3 minutes.

sessions.what: We ran one Quick enrichment in FullEnrich on its free credits on 13 November 2026 and read the billing screen. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We enriched no real person: the only record was a made-up contact at example.com, so the hit rate for mobile numbers was not tested. We did not use Download or Push to HubSpot, and we did not test checkout, support or cancellation.
findings: The home screen offers a Quick enrichment form with two checkboxes: Mobile phone at 10 credits and Work email at 1 credit. Only work email was ticked by default. You enter a LinkedIn URL or a name and company, or insert a row, or upload a CSV. The sidebar showed 50 credits left, expiring in 365 days, and no card was asked for.

We ticked both boxes for the made-up contact and pressed Enrich 1 contact. The result page said Running while the status moved through data sources, and after about three minutes it said Done 1/1: Phone Not found, Work Email Not found, 0 credits used. The balance stayed at 50.
So a failed lookup, even one that included a mobile number at 10 credits, cost nothing in this run. That is one made-up record, so it says nothing about charges for partial hits or about paid plans.

The billing screen priced 1,500 credits at €79.50 a month, with a yearly option 10% lower and three months of credit rollover. It lists a mobile phone at 10 credits (€0.53), a work email at 1 credit (€0.053) and a personal email at 3 credits (€0.159). That puts a work email near five cents at that size. The screen also says '80% find rate, 20+ data sources'. We did not test that claim.
